title.narrative: AFYA: Advancing Farmer & Youth Access to Healthcare

description.narrative: Smallholder coffee farmers in Uganda’s Greater Masaka region face structural challenges that threaten both their livelihoods and the long-term resilience of the coffee sector. With over 42% living below USD 2.15 per day and fewer than 1% covered by health insurance, a single medical emergency can force families to sell assets, pre-sell coffee at low prices, or pull children from school. These health-related income shocks reduce productivity, erode financial stability, and undermine farmer retention, posing a direct threat to supply chain sustainability.The Advancing Farmer & Youth Access to Healthcare (AFYA) project addresses these root causes by reaching +2,500 coffee farming families with access to a health program tailored to local needs. But AFYA is more than a service delivery effort. It aims to develop a long-term, locally anchored solution by embedding healthcare into the financial systems that farmers already trust: Savings and Credit Cooperative Organizations (SACCOs), VSLAs (Village Savings and Loan Associations), and emerging agri-fintech platforms. This enables households to cover healthcare premiums through flexible, harvest-aligned repayment models, avoiding the need for high-interest loans or harmful coping mechanisms.The project will focus on identifying which financing models are most inclusive, particularly for women, youth, and low-yield farmers. It will also define which healthcare services are most critical and explore whether participation in the program can help improve farmers’ credit profiles over time.By reducing the financial burden of illness, AFYA strengthens household resilience, expands access to credit, and supports more stable participation in cooperative systems. It positions healthcare not as a parallel intervention, but as a core enabler of economic security and the foundation for a more inclusive and resilient coffee sector - because in the end, healthy farmers mean stronger supply chains.
